faq.q: Why is a boat cruise good for Ironman Marbella recovery?
faq.a: After 3.8km swim, 180km bike, and 42.2km run, your muscles need gentle movement and relaxation. A boat cruise provides passive recovery: seated rest, light stretching, and the cooling sea breeze. The gentle rocking helps reduce muscle soreness, while the fresh air and Mediterranean views lower cortisol. Plus, you can elevate your legs and hydrate properly, which is exactly what your body needs.

faq.q: Which boat is best for a recovery cruise after Ironman Marbella?
faq.a: For a small group of 5–6, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are perfect for a quiet, low-key recovery. For up to 8–10, the Azimut 39 (11 pax) or Fairline Targa (10 pax) offer comfort and shade. If you want to celebrate with a bigger crew, the Mangusta 80 (12 pax) includes a jet ski – but note it has a 4-hour minimum.

faq.q: Can I watch the Ironman race from a boat?
faq.a: Yes, but you'll need to plan around the race route. The swim start and finish are in Marbella's bay, so a boat can anchor near the swim course (respecting official buoys). For the bike and run, you can't follow on water, but you can position near the coastline to see sections. A 2-hour morning cruise lets you catch the swim start, then return to shore to spectate on land.

faq.q: What's included in the charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). There are no hidden costs. For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39), the price is €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours. For the Mangusta 80, it's €4,719 for a minimum of 4 hours, with a free jet ski.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book for Ironman week?
faq.a: Ironman Marbella attracts thousands of athletes and spectators, so boats book out quickly. We recommend booking at least 2–3 weeks ahead, especially for the race weekend itself (usually late September). For the Mangusta 80, which is popular for group celebrations, book even earlier. Use WhatsApp for fastest confirmation and to secure your preferred time slot.

faq.q: Can I book a cruise for the day before the race?
faq.a: Absolutely – a pre-race cruise is a great way to relax and carb-load. A gentle 2-hour afternoon sail helps calm nerves and keeps your legs fresh. You can also use it to check out the swim course from the water. Many athletes find this mentally reassuring. Just avoid heavy sun exposure and alcohol; stick to the included water and soft drinks.

faq.q: What are the best local spots to visit on a recovery cruise?
faq.a: From Puerto Banús, head east towards Cabopino for calm coves like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés. These are sheltered, with clear water perfect for a gentle swim (if you feel up to it). Alternatively, cruise west towards Estepona or Sotogrande for longer, smoother runs. The skipper can adjust the route to your energy levels – just ask.

faq.q: Are there any restrictions for passengers after the race?
faq.a: No specific restrictions, but we advise caution with alcohol. Our boats include beer and cava, but after a full Ironman, your body is dehydrated and sensitive to alcohol. Stick to water and electrolyte drinks (we provide water and soft drinks). Also, remember to bring sunscreen and a light jacket – the sea breeze can feel cool after exertion.

data.body_html:
Ironman Marbella 2025 is more than a race – it's a weekend of endurance, adrenaline, and celebration. Whether you're crossing the finish line or cheering from the shore, the best way to recover is on the water. A recovery boat cruise from Puerto Banús offers athletes a chance to rest tired muscles, while fans can enjoy a unique spectator perspective. With our fleet departing from Puerto Banús, you're minutes away from the race action and the calm Mediterranean.

Why a Boat Cruise Is the Ultimate Recovery

After swimming 3.8km, cycling 180km, and running 42.2km, your body needs passive recovery. A boat cruise provides exactly that: you sit back, elevate your legs, and let the gentle motion of the sea soothe your muscles. The cool breeze (often 24–28°C in September) helps lower your core temperature, while the quiet of the open water reduces cortisol. Unlike a massage or foam rolling, a cruise is zero-effort – perfect for the day after the race.

Our Fleet for Recovery and Celebration

We have boats for every group size and budget. For a small, intimate recovery session, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are ideal. For couples or small groups, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) offer comfort and shade. If you're celebrating with a larger crew, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is a statement – and it comes with a free jet ski for a bit of fun, though it has a 4-hour minimum.

All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and Spanish IVA. No hidden extras.

Pricing for Ironman Week

BoatCapacityPrice
Astondoa 40 / Azimut 399–11 pax€749 (2h) – €2,299 (8h)

Other boats (Pershing 46, Ferretti 94, etc.)variesOn request via WhatsApp

For the best value, the Tier A boats are perfect for a 2–3 hour recovery cruise. If you want a full day of relaxation, the 8-hour option lets you explore as far as Estepona or Sotogrande.

Spectator Cruises: Watch the Race from the Sea

If you're supporting an athlete, a morning cruise offers a front-row seat to the swim start. The race typically begins around 7:00–8:00 AM in Marbella's bay. From our boats, you can anchor near the swim course (keeping clear of official markers) and watch the mass start – an unforgettable sight. After the swim, head back to shore to catch the bike and run sections. A 2-hour cruise works well, but a 4-hour option lets you combine spectating with a leisurely brunch onboard.

Best Local Routes for Recovery

For a gentle post-race cruise, we recommend heading east from Puerto Banús towards Cabopino. The coastline here is dotted with quiet coves like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés, where you can drop anchor and swim in calm, clear water. If you prefer a longer, smoother ride, head west towards Estepona or Sotogrande – the open sea is usually flat in September. Your skipper will adapt the route to your energy levels and preferences.

Tips for Athletes: What to Bring and Expect

  • Bring a light jacket – the sea breeze can feel cool after exertion.
  • Use sunscreen, even on cloudy days; the UV reflection off the water is strong.
  • Stay hydrated – we provide water and soft drinks, but bring electrolytes if you prefer.
  • Consider a gentle swim in a cove – the saltwater is therapeutic for sore muscles.
  • If you're prone to motion sickness, take medication beforehand; the bay is usually calm, but the open sea can be lively.

Booking Your Cruise for Ironman Marbella 2025

Race week is busy, so secure your boat early. The easiest way is to message us on WhatsApp – we'll confirm availability and pricing within minutes. For the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39, you can book directly at the fixed rates. For the Mangusta 80 or any other yacht, we'll send a tailored quote. All boats depart from Puerto Banús, just a 10-minute drive from Marbella's race village.

Make your Ironman weekend unforgettable – combine endurance with relaxation. Browse our full fleet and start planning your recovery cruise today.
